headline: Learned models predict compound activity, neurotoxicity and nanoparticle function
label: Machine Learning Compound Activity Prediction
summary: Curated databases and multimodal deep learning now support activity, toxicity and delivery prediction alongside generative molecular glue design.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned models linking molecular or formulation structure to biological or functional outcomes. NeuroTDPi fuses multimodal inputs in a deep network with SHAP interpretation, predicting neurotoxic compounds with AUC 0.82-0.97 and flagging structural alerts. LC-JT-VAE is generative, conditioning a junction tree variational autoencoder on ligase identity to produce synthesizable molecular glues that promote Abeta-42 degradation. NavDB and LNPDB supply the data substrate: NavDB curates 8023 records on 5168 voltage-gated sodium channel modulators and targets, while LNPDB consolidates structural and functional data for 19,528 lipid nanoparticles with standardized featurization and CHARMM lipid force fields. What is new here is ligase-conditioned generation with synthesizability constraints in LC-JT-VAE, and interpretable multimodal fusion paired with structural alerts in NeuroTDPi. The items are heterogeneous, so the shared thread is data-plus-model construction rather than a single method.
